{{Infobox character | name = Gossan | image = Gossan.png | race = Hearthian | planet = Timber Hearth | location = [[Timber_Hearth#Zero-G_Cave|Zero-G Cave]] }}__NOTOC__ '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is [[The Protagonist|the player]]'s flight instructor, zero-g coach, and one of the founding members of [[Outer Wilds Ventures]]. They are found at the entrance to the [[The Village#Zero-G Cave|Zero-G Cave]] before the [[Observatory]] and they are missing an eye alongside part of their left ear. They also used to pilot a ship but during their first trip they crashed into [[The Attlerock|the moon]]. Gossan used to work closely with [[Slate]], Outer Wilds' engineer, and [[Feldspar]], its best pilot, but now clashes with Slate over safety features regarding the spaceships. Gossan will direct the player to a nearby elevator to visit the Zero-G Cave for some practice with repairing a satellite. This functions as a tutorial for the player in learning how to repair their [[spaceship]] alongside moving in low gravity with [[Spacesuit|the Spacesuit]]. == Dialogue == === Introduction dialog === * “Hey, I thought I might see you before the big launch.
Nerves getting the better of you?” ** '''>Right, like you weren’t nervous for your first flight.''' *** “Hey, don’t worry about it. Your nerves are between you, me, and the vast endlessness of space.
But really, you’ll do fine out there. I’d worry more about that ship, if I were you. Hopefully that lunatic Slate at least fixed the retro rockets.” ****[[#Repair Satellite|repair satellite]] ** '''>I’m a little nervous, yeah.''' *** “Good. Everyone should be a bit nervous going into space. I got cocky during my first flight and nearly put a new crater in the moon.
Still, I was never as green as you.” **** '''>Hey, I’ve gotten better!''' ***** “Think so, do you? Feel like proving it to your old flight coach?
“There’s a “satellite” — which is definitely ''not'' just a piece of broken mining equipment — set up down in the zero-g cave and in need of repairs.
If you’re looking for a little last-minute zero-g practice, head down the lift and into the cave. Or don’t, so long as you’re confident you can make ship repairs in space.” ****** '''>One repaired “satellite,” coming up!''' ******* “Cool. Get to it, and try not to concuss yourself right before your first launch.” ****** '''>Nah, I’m ready for the real deal.''' ******* “Heh. Darn right you are.
Don’t get yourself killed out there, you hear? Not after I’ve put this much work into training you.
...Haha, go on, go make Outer Wilds Ventures proud.” **** '''>That’s not what Slate says...''' ***** “Oi, you know better than to believe a word that lunatic says about me.
They’re still sore I made them install a safety harness in the cockpit. Claimed it would “throw off the thrust-to-weight ratio.”
Honestly. One of these days I’m gonna throw off ''Slate’s'' thrust-to-weight ratio.” ******[[#Repair Satellite|repair satellite]] ** '''>Are you kidding? I’m a natural at this!''' *** “Is that so? Funny, I seem to recall the first time you strapped on a jetpack, we had to come fish you out of the crater near the south pole.” ****[[#Repair Satellite|repair satellite]] ==== Repair Satellite ==== * “So listen, there’s a “satellite” — which is definitely ''not'' just a piece of broken mining equipment — set up down in the zero-g cave and in need of repairs.
If you’re looking for a little last-minute zero-g practice, head down the lift and into the cave. Or don’t, so long as you’re confident you can make ship repairs in space.” ** '''>One repaired “satellite”, coming up!''' *** “Cool. Get to it, and try not to concuss yourself right before your first launch.” ** '''>Nah, I’m ready for the real deal.''' *** “Heh. Darn right you are.
Don’t get yourself killed out there, you hear? Not after I’ve put this much work into training you.
...Haha, go on, go make Outer Wilds Ventures proud.” === Follow-up dialog === (if the player told they weren't doing the repairs) * “If you changed your mind about practicing ship repairs, head down the lift and into the zero-g cave.
You just need to maneuver over to the “satellite” and repair each damaged area, same as you’ll be doing for your ship.” (if the player told they were doing the repairs) * “What’s the holdup? That “satellite” isn’t going to repair itself.
You just need to maneuver over to the “satellite” and repair each damaged area, same as you’ll be doing for your ship.” === After repairing the 'satellite' === * “Nicely done! Of course, it’ll be a little more stressful when you’re hurtling through space, but just remember your training and try not to hit anything big.
I can see you’re itching to get off this rock, so go get the launch codes from the observatory and get out of here already.
Best of luck out there! And hey, try to avoid getting yourself killed now that I’ve put so much time into training you, got it?” === After going to space === * “You’re back awfully soon. Everything alright? Slate didn’t do anything dumb like install a [[Spaceship#Eject Cockpit button|self-destruct button]], did they?” * === Followup Conversation (Waiting for satellite repair) === * What's the hold up? That "satellite" isn't going to repair itself.
You just need to maneuver over to the "satellite" and repair each damaged area, same as you'll be doing for your ship. === Followup Conversation (If having chosen 'real deal' response) === * If you changed your mind about practicing ship repairs, head down the lift and into the zero-g cave.
You just need to maneuver over to the "satellite" and repair each damaged area, same as you'll be doing for your ship. === Followup Conversation (After satellite is repaired) === * Nicely done! Of course, it'll be a little more stressful when you're hurtling through space, but just remember your training and try not to hit anything big.
I can see you're itching to get off the rock, so go get the launch codes from the observatory and get out of here already.
Best of luck out there! And hey, try to avoid getting yourself killed now that I've put so much time into training you, got it? == Alpha Version == [[File:Zerogcoach.png|thumb|354x354px|The coach standing in front of the Zero-G training area.]]During the alpha, Gossan was known as the '''Zero-G Coach'''. There is a dialog still present in the game files for when the player tried to go in the Cave without putting on the suit. Now the suit is inside the Cave ; * “Oi, don’t forget to put on a suit! I don’t want to have to come fish you out of there again.” == Trivia == * Gossan told [[Arkose]] that the patch of [[Ghost Matter]] in the village used to be bigger when Gossan was a hatchling. * [[Porphy]] suggests that the Protagonist, Gossan, and themself should open a bottle of The Good Stuff after their flight. Meanwhile, [[Esker]]'s signalscope log recommends that someone tell Gossan and Porphy "their flirting is ''not'' subtle from an aerial perspective." * Esker mentions being in touch with ground control -- "Hornfels and Gossan, mostly--" who sometimes radio up to chat. * Slate mentions Gossan's Zero-G training exercise, saying that the Protagonist doing a practice run there would "help to get Gossan off my back". They also say the risk of the ship log's destination markers "shorting out the fuel regulator and causing the ship to explode is so minimal that only Gossan would worry about it." * Gossan appears with all four eyes in the inaugural Outer Wilds founders' photo, indicating that the incident resulting in the loss of one of their eyes took place later than that. The "Self" ending implies that both the Protagonist and Slate had some involvement in the incident. "Self" cites it as a reason that Gossan and Slate never dated, and the Protagonist says they "very much do not want to discuss" what happened, with both swiftly agreeing to change the subject. * "Self" and the Protagonists also discuss how Gossan, unlike Slate, finds it a sign of a date going well when two people are talking and nothing has exploded yet. * Gossan has told [[Mica]] that if Mica ever designs a ship faster than Slate's ships, they should ask Slate to be their first test pilot. * According to Hornfels, Feldspar worked more closely with Gossan and Slate than with Hornfels themself due to their respective specialties. Still, Feldspar's journal entry about reaching the core of [[Giant's Deep]] noted their eagerness to tell Gossan and Hornfels about the adventure. * If the Protagonist tells Hornfels where Feldspar is, Hornfels excitedly plans to radio Gossan to prepare a ship and retrieve them, since "[i]t really should be Gossan who brings Feldspar home." * As all Hearthians they are named after minerals. [[wikipedia:Gossan|Gossan]] is intensely oxidized, weathered or decomposed rock, usually the upper and exposed part of an ore deposit or mineral vein. [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Hearthians]]
